axioms: TENSION (unresolved, this lens's home): measurement-validity thinking treats the record store as a faithful population and asks only whether the aggregation math is unbiased; flow/infrastructure thinking treats the gauge as merely 'exists / is aggregated' and asks only whether the channel has a relief path and a dredge cadence. Neither can see a gate whose metric is statistically sound over a sample the plumbing has silently biased, nor a spillway correctly designed whose diverted flow unbalances the sample the gate is calibrated against. This lens lives exactly there and does not resolve it.

A gating number is only as valid as the point in the flow where it is physically sampled: a gauge installed upstream of a fallback/escalation avulsion reads the pre-diversion intent, not the post-diversion reality the metric then trusts.

A designed relief path (fable->opus fallback, two-strikes escalation) is also a sampling mechanism: it systematically deposits the hardest/failed flow into one tier's record and the easy flow into another's, so the population the pass-rate metric aggregates is selected by the plumbing, not by tier capability.

Un-dredged evidence tables (routing_decisions, plan_execution_outcome) silt the channel bed until aggregation reads stale/partial/co-mingled data — the retention cadence is a measurement-validity control, not merely a storage concern.

The low-water pilot (2-3 items, Rule 6) is the most fragile flow AND the most underpowered sample; letting it feed the same calibrate loop that later gates live routing entrenches a cold-start reading taken at the worst moment for both flow-safety and statistical power.

Routing-that-consumes-the-metric is itself a spillway: a low/biased reading diverts flow away from a tier and thereby starves that tier of the samples needed to correct the estimate — a feedback trap that needs a minimum-flow/dredge guarantee neither parent lens alone would prescribe.

HARD CONSTRAINT: report a finding ONLY if it requires BOTH parent perspectives — every finding must name a flow/infrastructure mechanism AND a measurement-validity consequence for a gate, with an intersection_justification showing that deleting either half collapses the finding into a single-parent concern.
primitives: gauge-in-the-flow: a gate-governing number crossed with the point in the dispatch flow where it is physically sampled
spillway-as-sampler: fallback/escalation relief path treated as the selection mechanism that populates a tier's metric sample
silted denominator: un-dredged evidence-table growth producing a stale/partial/co-mingled aggregation population
avulsion-vs-gauge-placement: escalation/fallback tier-switch relative to where author_tier/executor_tier is recorded (attribution error from mis-placed gauge)
low-water-sample entrenchment: the 2-3-item pilot as both fragile flow and underpowered sample feeding the gating metric
starvation feedback loop: routing-consumes-metric as a spillway that drains the sample needed to correct a biased reading
lossy-gauge advancement: verdict-sidecar extraction as a fail-open reading that gates phase advance and feeds the metric
failure_mode: Declines any finding whose defect is purely statistical (bad aggregation math over a correctly-collected sample) — that belongs to fd-eval-calibration-metrics alone.
Declines any finding whose defect is purely hydraulic (missing relief path / dredge cadence with no downstream gate-corruption) — that belongs to fd-hydraulic-diversion alone.

Does not evaluate routing resolution/precedence determinism (fd-routing-kernel-mechanics), escalation state-machine termination (fd-escalation-retry-ladder), or authority/inspection-independence (fd-swordsmith-transmission); assumes those fire as designed and asks only whether their flow biases the sample a gating metric aggregates.

By construction cannot report a finding that only one parent lens would surface — the intersection-only constraint is the lens's failure mode when the two perspectives do not actually cross at a gated number.
